terms.boundary: It is not the unknowable historical original.
terms.definition: The standardized pre-damage digital image used for controlled comparison.
terms.label: Clean reference

terms.boundary: It is not a historical style, period or claim of cultural representation.
terms.definition: One of five balanced study groupings based on visible content.
terms.label: Broad visual category

terms.boundary: It does not reproduce every property of physical deterioration.
terms.definition: A repeatable digital mask or image change created for the experiment.
terms.label: Controlled synthetic damage

terms.boundary: Registration does not make the case eligible for every method.
terms.definition: One exact painting and controlled condition stored in the experiment registry.
terms.label: Registered case

terms.boundary: Eligibility is computational, not conservation approval.
terms.definition: A case all four full-scope methods were configured to process.
terms.label: Method-eligible case

terms.boundary: It is a technical control, not historical ground truth.
terms.definition: A zero-damage case used to check whether a method changes content unnecessarily.
terms.label: Unchanged control

terms.boundary: Candidate means available for inspection, not approved as correct.
terms.definition: One saved model output with an exact case and method identity.
terms.label: Restoration candidate

terms.boundary: Full scope does not mean the method is universally suitable.
terms.definition: A method evaluated across all 2,620 eligible cases.
terms.label: Full-scope method

terms.boundary: It is not a fifth full-scope comparison method.
terms.definition: A limited feasibility run with 35 scheduled cases and 24 completed outputs.
terms.label: Bounded SDXL branch

terms.boundary: Different metric families must not be merged into one universal score.
terms.definition: A group of measurements asking a related question about restoration behaviour.
terms.label: Metric family

terms.boundary: A metric is defensible only in a compatible region.
terms.definition: The part of the image where a measurement is intended to be interpreted.
terms.label: Evaluation region

terms.boundary: An anchor winner is not a universal best model.
terms.definition: One registered metric-and-region comparison used to compare methods.
terms.label: Quality anchor

terms.boundary: Their disagreement measures empirical variation, not calibrated confidence.
terms.definition: Four Stable Diffusion candidates sharing the same case and prompt but using different seeds.
terms.label: Repeated-seed group

terms.boundary: It is not a probability that a restoration is correct.
terms.definition: Observed variation among repeated supported Stable Diffusion outputs.
terms.label: Empirical uncertainty

terms.boundary: The fitted boundary is a review rule, not a failure probability.
terms.definition: The matched evidence population used to fit one warning or critical boundary.
terms.label: Threshold reference stratum

terms.boundary: It is not an expert verdict, trust score or conservation decision.
terms.definition: A rule-based signal showing which evidence needs closer inspection.
terms.label: Review flag

terms.boundary: It is not race, ethnicity or identity.
terms.definition: A measured image-lightness property used in the focused portrait audit.
terms.label: Rendered lightness

terms.boundary: A checksum confirms file identity, not scientific correctness.
terms.definition: A Git or Hugging Face object pinned by exact revision, size and checksum.
terms.label: Immutable source
